auditor-jane: Hi team — can you provide the documented procedure for KMS key access, recent RBAC change logs affecting key-encrypt/decrypt permissions, and a sample of audit logs showing an admin key rotation? We need this for SOC 2 evidence. Also curious: do you have an incident playbook that ties KMS compromise scenarios to forensics steps?
security-bot: New evidence request created: ticket #EVID-8742. Please add artifacts to /evidence/soc2/2026-03/KMS and tag with EVID-8742 :clipboard:
maria: Thanks — assigning. I'll pull the RBAC diffs and rotation audit. ETA EOD today.
oliver: Quick answers: KMS access is governed by IAM roles 'infra-kms-admin' and 'svc-redwood-enc'. We record rolebinding changes in git ops repo. Example rolebinding diff:
```
- role: cluster-admin
+ role: role/kms-encrypt-decrypt
  subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: svc-redwood-enc
```
Use git log in infra/roles/kms to show history.
aj: For audit logs, we forward CloudTrail -> S3 -> Splunk. Query we typically run:
```
index=kms sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail eventName=DisableKeyRotation OR eventName=ScheduleKeyDeletion userIdentity.arn=*
```
Return will include userIdentity, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters.
maria: I uploaded two artifacts: /evidence/soc2/2026-03/kms_access_procedure.md and /evidence/soc2/2026-03/rbac_change_manifest.csv — both include timestamps and signatures. Also attached a redacted CloudTrail sample showing rotation by oliver@redwood.com on 2026-03-12. Link: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/evidence/EVID-8742
auditor-jane: Thanks. Can you confirm retention windows (log retention), and whether keys have automated rotation enabled by default?
oliver: Retention: CloudTrail logs kept 3 years in S3 archival bucket (glacier after 90 days). Splunk hot/warm = 90 days, cold = 1 year, archived beyond. KMS keys: most customer keys created with automatic yearly rotation on; service keys are manually rotated per our playbook. See /runbooks/kms-rotation.md
maria: Confirmed. Also added a short mapping doc: control A.9 -> KMS key rotation evidence; control A.12 -> RBAC change logging. Uploaded to same folder.
auditor-jane: Good. One more: if a privileged service account is compromised, what's our incident escalation path and how do we prove chain of custody for key usage?
aj: Incident steps: 1) Isolate service account (revoke tokens, remove rolebindings), 2) Rotate affected keys (create new key and re-encrypt data), 3) Snapshot logs (CloudTrail + K8s audit), 4) Forensics team takes EBS snapshots. Chain of custody is in evidence manifest: who executed rotation, via which agent, artifacts signed by sigstore. Example CLI to list key policy changes:
```
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/redwood-service
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=DisableKeyRotation
```
maria: I'll add a timeline example for a simulated compromise we ran last quarter (redacted). Putting next to EVID-8742.
auditor-jane: Perfect. Can we get a high-level one-page summary mapping controls to artifacts for the auditor binder? Ideally by EOD Friday.
maria: Yep, I'll produce the binder summary and ping when done.
security-bot: Reminder: evidence ticket EVID-8742 will auto-close in 14 days if inactive.
auditor-jane: Thanks all :thumbsup:
